source.text: הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַ/גּ֔וֹי ל֖/וֹ הִגְדַּ֣לְתָּ הַ/שִּׂמְחָ֑ה שָׂמְח֤וּ לְ/פָנֶ֨י/ךָ֙ כְּ/שִׂמְחַ֣ת בַּ/קָּצִ֔יר כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגִ֖ילוּ בְּ/חַלְּקָ֥/ם שָׁלָֽל׃
source.note: WLC/OSHB Masoretic reading form: this draft selects the explicitly recorded qere ל֖/וֹ ('to it') in place of written לא ('not'); all other source text is retained. This is not the ketiv-only string or a transcription of 1QIsa-a. Source priority remains provisional.
source.numbering_note: POB/WLC Isaiah 9:2 corresponds to Isaiah 9:3 in many English Bibles and the selected Latin edition.

apparatus.note: Written negative retained as alternative; exact old source preserved in review_history and application receipt.
Selected Masoretic reading, preposition with third-person masculine singular suffix; the preceding nation supplies its beneficiary.
Unbracketed published spelling; same-scroll uses have both negative and beneficiary senses. It does not independently establish the selected meaning; no fresh pixel reading.
Selected Latin negative interpretation, contrary versional evidence; not a surviving Hebrew exemplar.
Selected positive-joy wording within a divergent opening; 'your joy' does not recover exact Hebrew לו.

translation.text: You have multiplied the nation; you have increased its joy[a]. They rejoice before you as with the joy at harvest[b], as men exult when they divide spoil.

footnotes.text: The draft follows the Masoretic qere (reading tradition), 'to it': 'you have increased its joy.' The written Hebrew has 'not': 'you have not increased the joy,' also reflected in the selected Weber/Gryson Latin text. The published 1QIsa-a spelling לוא can express either sense. The selected Greek portrays joy positively but has a different construction and 'your joy'; it does not establish exact Hebrew לו. The earlier wording remains unresolved.
Or 'they rejoice before you like the joy of harvest, like people rejoicing when they divide plunder.'

lexical_decisions.rationale: Hiphil of רבה commonly means to make many or multiply. 'Have multiplied' preserves the causative sense and fits the direct object 'the nation.'
גוי can mean nation or people. In this context, singular 'the nation' best matches the Hebrew form and the prophetic image of a corporate people enlarged.

alternatives: you have not increased the joy (written לא)
for it you have made the joy great
lexical_decisions.lexicon: WLC/OSHB written/read record and selected versional editions (no fresh lexicon consultation)
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected WLC qere is a preposition with third-person masculine singular suffix, not the written negative. Its beneficiary can be the immediately preceding singular nation; 'its joy' expresses that relation naturally. Positive growth and joy fit the immediate celebration and following deliverance explanations. Written לא and the selected Latin negative remain substantial alternatives; 1QIsa-a spelling is nondiscriminating and selected Greek is syntactically divergent. This is a provisional source choice, not an English-only deletion of 'not' or an earliest-wording proof.
Qal perfect 3cp from שמח denotes rejoicing. Present English 'rejoice' works well in prophetic discourse to express the vivid result without awkwardness.
Literally 'before your face/presence.' 'Before you' is natural English and preserves the Godward orientation of the joy.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as with the joy at harvest
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase compares their rejoicing to harvest-time joy. 'At harvest' is idiomatic and clear.

The verb גיל conveys exuberant rejoicing or exultation. 'Exult' preserves the heightened tone. Supplying 'men' reflects the masculine plural verbal form in a generic sense, in keeping with the gender-accurate policy.
The idiom refers to distributing captured goods after victory. 'Spoil' is a standard, readable rendering that preserves the martial image.

theological_decisions.issue: Textual reading of לא ('not') versus לו ('to it/him') in the second colon
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Select the recorded Masoretic qere לו provisionally, rendered 'you have increased its joy.'
alternative_readings: Written לא: 'you have not increased the joy'
Qere literally: 'for it you have made the joy great'
theological_decisions.rationale: Source selection follows the paragraph's light, joy and deliverance movement, not compulsory written-form priority or theological preference. The written negative and selected Latin support remain real counterevidence; the earlier scroll spelling can express either sense, and the Greek cannot recover exact לו. The qere could be a contextual repair of a harder negative. Preserve the negative in the reader note and apparatus; do not claim historical certainty, newly recovered letters or fresh lexicon consultation.

value.rationale: The Hebrew source provided is the MT and plainly reads לֹא ('not'). Although the sense is difficult in context and many witnesses/versions support a reading equivalent to לו ('to it'), the translation should not silently emend the text. The smoother alternative is preserved in a footnote as a textual variant.
value.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: Original-language primacy over translation tradition; preserve ambiguity/tension rather than resolve it silently.
